name: arc-panel-replication
description: Solve ARC grids divided by uniform separator lines where one panel contains a pattern and the other panels copy it.

# ARC Panel Replication

Use this procedure when a grid is partitioned by straight, uniform separator lines and one panel contains a pattern while other panels are blank.

1. Identify the separator color and locate complete horizontal and vertical separator lines; verify the resulting panels have matching dimensions.
2. Compare the panel interiors, treating the uniform background as blank, and identify the single panel containing the motif; preserve its exact cell coordinates and colors.
3. Copy the motif at the same local coordinates into every blank panel, leaving each separator line unchanged; keep all other background cells as they are.
4. Check that each panel has the same local pattern and that the output dimensions and separator positions match the input before submitting.

In a demonstrated case, a 14x7 grid had 4-row panels separated by full-width color-4 rows; the 4x7 pattern in the first panel was copied to the other two. A second case had a 2x8 motif in one panel of a 2x3 panel arrangement, replicated to the other five panels while keeping the color-4 dividers intact.
",
 "reason": "Requested saving useful knowledge from the solved instance for future related ARC instances."
}

description: Solve Continual-ARC square-grid expansion tasks where demos double the grid into four rotated copies.

# ARC rotation tiling

1. Compare demo dimensions and quadrants. Use this rule when an N×N input becomes 2N×2N, the top-left quadrant is unchanged, and the other quadrants match rotations of that same input.
2. For input `A`, form quadrants in this order: top-left `A`; top-right 90° clockwise; bottom-left 90° counter-clockwise; bottom-right 180°. Concatenate the two quadrants row-by-row; do not recolor or alter cells.
3. Validate each rotated quadrant against at least one demo, especially with an asymmetric input; check dimensions are 2N×2N and the top-left exactly equals the input before submitting.

# ARC template recoloring

1. Read the current input and demos. Identify the marker shape and target color from this instance; normalize marker coordinates to its top-left. Treat diagonal contacts as connected only when the examples support that interpretation.
2. Apply the demonstrated matching rule: find translations of the marker template whose cells all have the target color, and recolor exactly those cells to the marker color. Do not rotate or reflect the template unless demos establish it.
3. Validate on a demo: the changed cells must equal the union of all matched placements, and every other cell must stay unchanged. If not, revise the rule or request another demo only to resolve the ambiguity.
4. Check dimensions and every output row, then end with exactly one valid action JSON object on the last line.
